question.text: How close to the curb should you parallel park?

answer.text: Where parallel parking is allowed, park within twelve inches of the curb, or as near as possible to the outer edge of the shoulder, so traffic is not blocked or slowed.

teaching.text: Park within twelve inches of the curb, or close to the shoulder's edge, so traffic keeps moving. Remember: within a foot of curb.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Where parallel parking is allowed, park within twelve inches of the curb, or as near as possible to the outer edge of the shoulder, so traffic is not blocked or slowed.

question.text: Parked facing downhill at a curb, which way do the front wheels point?

answer.text: Parked facing downhill beside a curb, turn the front wheels toward the curb and let the car roll gently until the front tire rests against it.

teaching.text: Facing downhill at a curb, wheels turn toward it and the front tire rests against it. Remember: downhill, wheels to curb.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Parked facing downhill beside a curb, turn the front wheels toward the curb and let the car roll gently until the front tire rests against it.

question.text: Parked facing uphill at a curb, which way do the front wheels point?

answer.text: Parked facing uphill beside a curb, point the front wheels away from it and ease backward until the rear of the front tire is blocked by the curb.

teaching.text: Facing uphill at a curb, wheels turn away and the curb blocks the back of the front tire. Remember: uphill, wheels away.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Parked facing uphill beside a curb, point the front wheels away from it and ease backward until the rear of the front tire is blocked by the curb.

question.text: With no curb, which way do you turn the front wheels on a hill?

answer.text: With no curb, turn the front wheels to the right whether facing uphill or downhill, so a rolling car would leave the highway instead of entering traffic.

teaching.text: With no curb, wheels go right either way, so a rolling car leaves the highway. Remember: no curb, turn right.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: With no curb, turn the front wheels to the right whether facing uphill or downhill, so a rolling car would leave the highway instead of entering traffic.

question.text: How do the three hill parking rules differ?

answer.text: With a curb, downhill means wheels toward the curb and uphill means wheels away from it; without a curb, the wheels go right either way.

teaching.text: Name the case first: downhill toward, uphill away, no curb right. Remember: toward, away, or right.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: With a curb, downhill means wheels toward the curb and uphill means wheels away from it; without a curb, the wheels go right either way.

question.text: Why are freeways dangerous?

answer.text: Freeways are dangerous because of the high speeds involved, so stay aware of everything around you at all times.

teaching.text: High speeds make freeways dangerous, so stay aware of everything around you. Remember: high speed, full awareness.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Freeways are dangerous because of the high speeds involved, so stay aware of everything around you at all times.

question.text: What are freeways built to do?

answer.text: Freeways are built to carry more traffic at higher speeds than ordinary streets or highways.

teaching.text: Freeways carry more traffic at higher speeds than ordinary roads. Remember: more traffic, higher speeds.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Freeways are built to carry more traffic at higher speeds than ordinary streets or highways.

question.text: What should you do on an acceleration ramp?

answer.text: On an acceleration ramp, build up speed to match freeway traffic before you merge.

teaching.text: Use the acceleration ramp to reach freeway speed before merging. Remember: match freeway speed first.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: On an acceleration ramp, build up speed to match freeway traffic before you merge.

question.text: How do you enter from a side entrance ramp?

answer.text: To enter from a side entrance ramp, signal, look for a gap, speed up to the traffic speed and merge only when it is safe.

teaching.text: Signal, find a gap, match traffic speed, and merge only when safe. Remember: signal, gap, speed, merge.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: To enter from a side entrance ramp, signal, look for a gap, speed up to the traffic speed and merge only when it is safe.

question.text: When may you merge from the acceleration lane, and who has the right of way?

answer.text: Do not merge until the solid white line ends, avoid stopping in the acceleration lane unless truly necessary, and remember that freeway traffic has the right-of-way.

teaching.text: Wait for the solid white line to end, avoid stopping, and yield to freeway traffic. Remember: wait for the white line.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Do not merge until the solid white line ends, avoid stopping in the acceleration lane unless truly necessary, and remember that freeway traffic has the right-of-way.

question.text: What do you do on a metered entrance ramp?

answer.text: On a metered entrance ramp, stop at the signal and enter the freeway only when released by a green light.

teaching.text: At a ramp meter, stop and go only on green. Remember: green light releases you.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: On a metered entrance ramp, stop at the signal and enter the freeway only when released by a green light.

question.text: When is stopping on an entrance ramp the right move?

answer.text: When entering a freeway you match its speed and yield to it; stopping in the acceleration lane is a last resort, except on a metered ramp where you stop for the signal.

teaching.text: Stopping on a ramp is a last resort, except at a meter. Remember: stop only at meters.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When entering a freeway you match its speed and yield to it; stopping in the acceleration lane is a last resort, except on a metered ramp where you stop for the signal.

question.text: Which freeway lane should you use when going slower than traffic?

answer.text: Use the rightmost lane when you are going slower than normal traffic speed.

teaching.text: Drivers going slower than traffic belong in the rightmost lane. Remember: slow drivers keep right.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Use the rightmost lane when you are going slower than normal traffic speed.

question.text: What is the leftmost freeway lane for?

answer.text: The leftmost passing lane is for passing, left turns, and times when heavy traffic leaves no room to merge into the other lanes.

teaching.text: The leftmost lane is for passing, left turns, and heavy traffic with no room elsewhere. Remember: left lane for passing.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The leftmost passing lane is for passing, left turns, and times when heavy traffic leaves no room to merge into the other lanes.

question.text: How do the rightmost and leftmost freeway lanes differ?

answer.text: The rightmost freeway lane is for slower drivers, while the leftmost lane is reserved for passing, left turns and heavy-traffic situations.

teaching.text: Slower drivers keep right; the left lane is for passing. Remember: right slow, left passing.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The rightmost freeway lane is for slower drivers, while the leftmost lane is reserved for passing, left turns and heavy-traffic situations.

question.text: What should you do as you approach a merge area?

answer.text: Approaching a merge area, move over when it is safe to give entering vehicles room.

teaching.text: Near a merge, move over when safe so entering drivers have room. Remember: make room for mergers.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Approaching a merge area, move over when it is safe to give entering vehicles room.

question.text: What should you watch on the freeway?

answer.text: On the freeway, watch traffic ahead, beside and behind you, stay aware of vehicles in your blind spots, and plan ahead with directional and guide signs.

teaching.text: Watch ahead, beside and behind, mind your blind spots, and plan with guide signs. Remember: ahead, beside, behind.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: On the freeway, watch traffic ahead, beside and behind you, stay aware of vehicles in your blind spots, and plan ahead with directional and guide signs.

question.text: What are the freeway lane-change rules?

answer.text: On the freeway, signal at least two hundred feet before a lane change, avoid changing lanes often, and never drive across, over or inside a median or island.

teaching.text: Signal two hundred feet ahead, change lanes rarely, and never cross a median. Remember: signal early, change rarely.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: On the freeway, signal at least two hundred feet before a lane change, avoid changing lanes often, and never drive across, over or inside a median or island.

question.text: How do you use the deceleration lane to exit?

answer.text: To exit, use the deceleration lane: signal two hundred feet before it begins, hold your speed until you are in it, then slow to the advised exit ramp speed.

teaching.text: Signal two hundred feet before the deceleration lane, hold speed until in it, then slow. Remember: hold speed, then slow.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: To exit, use the deceleration lane: signal two hundred feet before it begins, hold your speed until you are in it, then slow to the advised exit ramp speed.

question.text: Where do you slow down when exiting a freeway?

answer.text: On the exit you keep your speed until inside the deceleration lane and slow down there, not on the freeway itself.

teaching.text: The slowdown happens in the deceleration lane, not on the freeway. Remember: slow in the exit lane.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: On the exit you keep your speed until inside the deceleration lane and slow down there, not on the freeway itself.

question.text: What should you avoid when leaving a freeway?

answer.text: When leaving a freeway, keep pace with traffic until the exit, do not exit at the last second, and do not exceed the posted ramp limit.

teaching.text: Keep pace until the exit, never exit at the last second, and obey the ramp limit. Remember: no last-second exits.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When leaving a freeway, keep pace with traffic until the exit, do not exit at the last second, and do not exceed the posted ramp limit.

question.text: What counts as a lane change, and what does each one require?

answer.text: A lane change includes moving between lanes, passing, merging from an entrance ramp and pulling onto the road from a curb or shoulder, and each requires checking ahead, beside and behind.

teaching.text: Lane changes include passing, merging and pulling out from a curb, and all need full checks. Remember: every move needs checking.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A lane change includes moving between lanes, passing, merging from an entrance ramp and pulling onto the road from a curb or shoulder, and each requires checking ahead, beside and behind.

question.text: What is a blind spot?

answer.text: A blind spot is an area slightly to the side and rear of your vehicle that neither the rearview nor side mirrors show.

teaching.text: The blind spot sits slightly to the side and rear, where no mirror reaches. Remember: mirrors miss this spot.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A blind spot is an area slightly to the side and rear of your vehicle that neither the rearview nor side mirrors show.

question.text: Why are mirrors not enough for a lane change?

answer.text: Mirrors are not enough for a lane change, because the blind spot just behind and beside you needs an over-the-shoulder look.

teaching.text: Only a look over your shoulder covers the blind spot. Remember: look over your shoulder.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Mirrors are not enough for a lane change, because the blind spot just behind and beside you needs an over-the-shoulder look.

question.text: What is the lane-change routine?

answer.text: To change lanes, signal for at least three seconds or two hundred feet, check ahead, check the mirrors, look over your shoulder at the blind spot, then move over when safe.

teaching.text: Signal three seconds or two hundred feet, check ahead and mirrors, look over your shoulder, then move. Remember: signal, mirrors, shoulder, move.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: To change lanes, signal for at least three seconds or two hundred feet, check ahead, check the mirrors, look over your shoulder at the blind spot, then move over when safe.

question.text: What should you do once you are in the new lane?

answer.text: Once centered in the new lane, glance at the mirror for traffic behind you, and switch the signal off no more than three seconds after the change is complete.

teaching.text: Once centered, check the mirror and cancel the signal within three seconds. Remember: check mirror, cancel signal.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Once centered in the new lane, glance at the mirror for traffic behind you, and switch the signal off no more than three seconds after the change is complete.

question.text: How long before and after a lane change does the signal run?

answer.text: The lane-change signal runs at least three seconds or two hundred feet before you move, and goes off within three seconds after you finish.

teaching.text: Signal early before the move and cancel promptly after. Remember: signal before, cancel after.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The lane-change signal runs at least three seconds or two hundred feet before you move, and goes off within three seconds after you finish.

question.text: Where is passing normally done, and what shows where it is allowed?

answer.text: Signs and markings show where passing is and is not allowed, and passing is normally done on the left.

teaching.text: Signs and markings show where to pass, and passing is normally on the left. Remember: pass on the left.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Signs and markings show where passing is and is not allowed, and passing is normally done on the left.

question.text: When is passing on the right allowed, and when is it never allowed?

answer.text: Passing on the right is allowed only on one-way streets and on roads with two or more lanes each way, and passing by driving off the pavement or on the shoulder is never allowed.

teaching.text: Right-side passing needs a one-way street or two or more lanes each way, and never the shoulder. Remember: never pass on shoulders.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Passing on the right is allowed only on one-way streets and on roads with two or more lanes each way, and passing by driving off the pavement or on the shoulder is never allowed.

question.text: Which right-side passing is allowed, and which is never allowed?

answer.text: Passing on the right is allowed on one-way streets and roads with two or more lanes each way, but passing on the shoulder or off the pavement never is.

teaching.text: The shoulder is never a passing lane. Remember: right sometimes, shoulder never.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Passing on the right is allowed on one-way streets and roads with two or more lanes each way, but passing on the shoulder or off the pavement never is.

question.text: What must you judge before passing anyone?

answer.text: Before passing anyone, bicyclists included, judge from traffic ahead, beside and behind whether you have enough time and room to do it safely.

teaching.text: Before any pass, judge time and room from traffic ahead, beside and behind. Remember: enough time and room.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Before passing anyone, bicyclists included, judge from traffic ahead, beside and behind whether you have enough time and room to do it safely.

question.text: How many vehicles should you pass at once?

answer.text: Pass only one vehicle at a time rather than counting on passing several at once.

teaching.text: Pass one vehicle at a time. Remember: one at a time.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Pass only one vehicle at a time rather than counting on passing several at once.

question.text: How do you know when to return to your lane after passing?

answer.text: To pass, change lanes properly, speed up past the vehicle, and return to your lane once both of its headlights appear in your rearview mirror.

teaching.text: Speed past, then return when both headlights show in your mirror. Remember: both headlights in mirror.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: To pass, change lanes properly, speed up past the vehicle, and return to your lane once both of its headlights appear in your rearview mirror.

question.text: How far from oncoming vehicles must you be when you finish a pass?

answer.text: Never start a pass unless you can be back on the right side while still more than two hundred feet from any oncoming vehicle, counting a bicyclist on the oncoming lane or shoulder.

teaching.text: Be back on the right side while more than two hundred feet from oncoming traffic, bicyclists included. Remember: finish well before oncoming.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Never start a pass unless you can be back on the right side while still more than two hundred feet from any oncoming vehicle, counting a bicyclist on the oncoming lane or shoulder.

question.text: When must you not start a pass because of a solid yellow line?

answer.text: Do not pass if you cannot get back to the right side before a solid yellow line begins.

teaching.text: Skip the pass if you cannot get back before a solid yellow line begins. Remember: back before solid yellow.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Do not pass if you cannot get back to the right side before a solid yellow line begins.

question.text: What two conditions tell you a pass is properly finished?

answer.text: Return to your lane after passing when you see both headlights of the passed vehicle in the rearview mirror, and finish before a solid yellow line begins.

teaching.text: A finished pass means both headlights in the mirror and back before solid yellow. Remember: headlights seen, before yellow.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Return to your lane after passing when you see both headlights of the passed vehicle in the rearview mirror, and finish before a solid yellow line begins.

question.text: How much room must you leave when passing a bicyclist?

answer.text: When passing a bicyclist, keep at least three feet between the rider and the outermost part of your vehicle, including mirrors or a trailer.

teaching.text: Measure three feet from the rider to your vehicle's outermost part, mirrors and trailer included. Remember: three feet, mirrors included.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When passing a bicyclist, keep at least three feet between the rider and the outermost part of your vehicle, including mirrors or a trailer.

question.text: When may you cross a solid yellow line to pass a bicyclist?

answer.text: To pass a bicyclist you may briefly cross a solid yellow line when no traffic is oncoming and your view ahead is clear.

teaching.text: Cross a solid yellow line briefly for a bicyclist only with no oncoming traffic and a clear view. Remember: clear road, brief crossing.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: To pass a bicyclist you may briefly cross a solid yellow line when no traffic is oncoming and your view ahead is clear.

question.text: When should you give bicyclists extra room?

answer.text: Give bicyclists extra room on rural roads, in a large vehicle or in wind, because a wind blast can knock a rider over.

teaching.text: Rural roads, large vehicles and wind all call for extra room. Remember: wind can topple riders.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Give bicyclists extra room on rural roads, in a large vehicle or in wind, because a wind blast can knock a rider over.

hooks_spoken: Match freeway speed on the ramp, merge after the solid white line ends, and stop only at a ramp meter.
recap.narration_text: Time for a quick review of entering a freeway. Match freeway speed on the ramp, merge after the solid white line ends, and stop only at a ramp meter. Keep these ideas handy as you practice.

hooks_spoken: Keep right when slower, use the left lane for passing, and make room at merges.
recap.narration_text: Time for a quick review of freeway lanes and awareness. Keep right when slower, use the left lane for passing, and make room at merges. Keep these ideas handy as you practice.

recap.narration_text: Time for a quick review of exiting a freeway. Hold your speed until you are in the deceleration lane, then slow to the ramp speed. Keep these ideas handy as you practice.

hooks_spoken: Signal, check mirrors, look over your shoulder, then move, and cancel the signal soon after.
recap.narration_text: Time for a quick review of changing lanes. Signal, check mirrors, look over your shoulder, then move, and cancel the signal soon after. Keep these ideas handy as you practice.

hooks_spoken: Pass on the left; pass on the right only where allowed, and never on the shoulder.
recap.narration_text: Time for a quick review of when and where to pass. Pass on the left; pass on the right only where allowed, and never on the shoulder. Keep these ideas handy as you practice.

hooks_spoken: Return when both headlights show in your mirror, and finish before any solid yellow line.
recap.narration_text: Time for a quick review of completing a pass. Return when both headlights show in your mirror, and finish before any solid yellow line. Keep these ideas handy as you practice.
